contentDesign.job_story: When finishing this physics course, I want to understand how the mechanical, electromagnetic and quantum pictures developed, so I can connect the ideas I have learned without mistaking an old model for an exact modern law.
contentDesign.reader: The charter's young, capable independent learner; reading needs inferred from the source and the direct authoring assignment, not user testing.
contentDesign.one_question: How do different physical theories connect the many phenomena in the world?
priority: Keep the source's opening connection to the course.
Follow the actual historical sequence: mechanical picture, electromagnetic picture, common constituents, interactions, quantum principles, open questions.
Put each needed modern qualification beside the historical claim it qualifies.
Preserve the source's quotations as the textbook's attributed wording, not as newly verified archival quotations.
contentDesign.form: Source-bound explanatory prose; the same twenty-six entries, short final-flow paragraphs and concept boundaries. No exercises, figures, marketing copy or process instructions.
dropped_for_lack_of_evidence: No new archival quotation attribution, date or citation.
No forecast for when a unified theory will be discovered.
No newly invented measurements, numerical examples or exercises.
contentDesign.independent_copy_review: Pending ZHEN gate; author decisions are not independent review.

cern-standard-model.locator: Matter particles; Forces and carrier particles; So far so good, but...
cern-standard-model.use: Quarks/leptons, distinct interactions and carriers, Standard Model scope, gravity exclusion and unanswered questions.
cern-standard-model.limits: The page includes older Higgs-discovery language, which is not used. No claim that every paragraph is a current research update.

einstein-relativistic-mechanics.locator: A question of velocities; Step by step from Newton to Einstein
einstein-relativistic-mechanics.use: Nonrelativistic/weak-gravity limiting domain and the need for relativistic corrections.
einstein-relativistic-mechanics.limits: No numerical orbital examples or discovery-timing claims are used.

feynman-electromagnetic-propagation.use: Field changes depend on earlier source behaviour, not instantaneous electromagnetic influence.
feynman-electromagnetic-propagation.limits: Only the established classical electromagnetic relation is used; this is not an assertion of a complete modern theory.

nuclear-forces-primary.locator: Abstract plus fulltext introductory observation receipt nuclear-forces-fulltext
nuclear-forces-primary.use: Low-energy effective nuclear-force account, useful pion exchange, and distinction from underlying QCD.
nuclear-forces-primary.limits: Abstract alone is insufficient for pion exchange. Its evidence binding includes the separately observed author fulltext introductory passages.

nuclear-forces-fulltext.use: Author manuscript distinctions between meson models, pion/nucleon effective degrees of freedom, and quark/gluon QCD.
nuclear-forces-fulltext.limits: Established model/domain distinction, not the latest review or every formula in the manuscript.

feynman-quantum-behaviour.locator: 1-1 Atomic mechanics; 1-4 electron interference; 1-7 probability amplitudes
feynman-quantum-behaviour.use: Quantum behaviour is not a literal classical ball-or-wave picture; outcome probabilities and microscopic domain.
feynman-quantum-behaviour.limits: Historical lecture examples are used only for established quantum principles, not contemporary particle inventories.

feynman-state-evolution.locator: 8-2; 8-4 How states change with time; 8-5 the Hamiltonian matrix; 8-6 ammonia example
feynman-state-evolution.use: State amplitudes evolve by an equation; an example probability reaches certainty, qualifying blanket unpredictability. A hydrogen example has a proton and an electron.
feynman-state-evolution.limits: The lecture has outdated discussion of unknown proton structure, which is not used; constituent correction uses CERN and Fermilab instead.

coherent-weak-scattering.locator: COHERENT collaboration original experimental abstract, arXiv:1708.01294
coherent-weak-scattering.use: Observed elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering is a Standard Model interaction without requiring particle transformation.
coherent-weak-scattering.limits: Its weak-interaction interpretation is read together with the CERN carrier account; the learner text does not import any experimental numbers.

fermilab-beta-decay-retained.locator: Retained primary-source receipt, All Things Neutrino: Neutrinos from beta decay
fermilab-beta-decay-retained.use: Composite proton/neutron constituents, beta-minus products and conservation conditions.
fermilab-beta-decay-retained.limits: Reuse is a source receipt, not an inherited N151 SCI verdict or archival source proof.
